title: bn254-pairing-inversion: gated tag-walk rho (a walk step is an inner product on 64-bit words), expected work, output ([x]P0, Q0)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and z=g^x in the protected BN254 target group GT, g=e(P0,Q0), the algorithm in proof.md returns P=[x]P0 in G1 and Q=Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z (for z=1: P=infinity and Q=Q0) with success at least 0.39, as algorithmic probability over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, under the disclosed heuristics H1 (an opened run that is never capped finds x after at most 107/100 times sqrt(pi r m/(2(m-1))) walk steps in expectation, m=6), H2 (on elements visited for the first time, the distinguished set and the uncertified tags are hit at their natural rates to within a stated factor) and H3 (at most 2^98 evaluations of already visited elements in expectation), supported by a proved tag lemma, algebra on the pinned constants and full-algorithm toy runs. Before any other work the algorithm reads one fresh 64-bit coin u and opens the run only when u < K, K = 7229537559736918267, the least integer for which the opened share of runs times the supported success of an opened run reaches 0.39; a closed run costs 64 instructions and is counted as a failure. An opened run finds x by a sequential distinguished-point Pollard rho walk in GT with 6 multipliers g^c z^d: the next multiplier is read from one stored coordinate of the current element, a step computes a 64-bit tag as the inner product of 72 stored 43-bit digits with 72 table words and uses it only when the tag certifies the exact selector (proof.md section 2), the table holds every product of at most 1,024 multipliers, one Fp12 product re-bases the element every 1,024 steps, uncertified elements are evaluated exactly, distinguished elements (90 bits) go to an ordered store keyed by the whole element, and g^x=z is checked before output; it continues until it finds x or a counter reaches its cap. The score is an expectation: the expected total computation over the same uniform challenges and fresh coins is at most 2^119.067296 target-group-operation equivalents (scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents divided by C=20,000). It is not a bound on every run: on every run the total computation is at most 2^128.708866 equivalents, enforced by counters (a trip budget of 1,025 per call of the step loop, a 3-word exit counter compared with its cap at every exit, 2^50 walk starts, 2^50 reports, 16 recoveries). Prices are executed instruction counts of generated AArch64 programs: 145 instructions per walk step and 15,158 per exit from the step loop (one Fp12 product of 13,843 with the label additions, digits and counters, plus a stated allowance). Both totals include the gate, all input checks, constants, the table construction, fresh coins (16 instructions per 64-bit word), walk starts, reports, store operations, recoveries, verification, the scalar multiplication and pairing check of the output. Peak memory is at most 2^61.007988 bytes in one address space with 64-bit pointers; preprocessing is at most 2^56.249959 equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Nothing is amortised over other targets, and no prior acceptance, submission or score is a premise. Analytic exploratory claim: no production-size run, not a finite-field sieve estimate.

experiments.purpose: Generate and execute the priced AArch64 programs (Fp multiply/add/sub, Fp12 product, the walk's step loop on real windows, the re-base with its counters on both sides of both caps, both sides of the certificate threshold, the trip budget) against big-integer arithmetic and print executed counts; check the tag lemma and the certified-selector corollary on production-size values; recompute every ledger integer, the gate constant K (and that K - 1 fails), the expected and every-run totals and the score; execute the output step P=[x]P0; run the complete algorithm of proof.md to its output in the BN-family toy field q=p(-15), r'=r(-15). Toy results are evidence at toy scale only.
